sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He would further submit that the victim/prosecutrix was a consenting party and on her own will she left her parental house and stayed with the appellant for about one month.
He would further submit that the doctor who examined the victim prosecutrix has opined that (MLC report Ex-P/18) there is no sign and symptoms of recent sexual intercourse.
He would submit that the appellant is in jail since 26.01.2021, hence, he may be released on bail.
On the other hand, Shri HS Ahluwalia, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail.

He would further submit that the appellant has allured the minor girl, aged about 13 years and 6 months at the time of incident, on the pretext of marriage, took her to various places and established physical relationship with her.
Hence, there is sufficient evidence against the appellant to connect him with crime in question.
Therefore, the appellant is not liable to be released on bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly considering the manner in which the appellant took the minor prosecutrix, below the age of 16 years, to various places and sexually exploited her for about one month on the pretext of marriage, we are of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to suspend the jail sentences.
Accordingly, IA No. 1 of 2023 stands rejected.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing after four weeks.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (NK Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
